definition: Role family covering robotics engineering positions. Key skills: SLAM, perception, computer vision, ROS/ROS2, C++, sensor fusion, navigation, motion planning, embedded systems. Relevant companies: Boston Dynamics, Skydio, Nuro, iRobot, Covariant, Amazon Robotics, Toyota Research Institute.

Role family covering data science and ML positions. Key skills: machine learning, Python, SQL, statistics, experimentation, A/B testing, recommendation systems, NLP, deep learning, feature engineering. Range from product analytics roles to research-heavy ML scientist roles.

Role family covering backend and platform engineering positions. Key skills: Go, Python, Java, distributed systems, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kubernetes, microservices, API design, gRPC. Often includes on-call responsibilities and production ownership.

Default outreach tone for most engineering roles. Characteristics: respectful, concise, highlights role specifics and company strengths, avoids overly casual language. Appropriate for senior candidates and most corporate/enterprise contexts.

Outreach tone for highly technical candidates (staff+ engineers, researchers). Characteristics: leads with technical challenge or problem space, mentions tech stack specifics, references candidate's published work or open-source contributions. Avoids generic company pitches.
